method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING-kind where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; two regulative rules (s 10(1) the proper authority notifies the informant within 3 months; s 17(1)(a) the informant supplies requested information within the period specified) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

seat: the person who makes a disclosure (the informant): any person, usually a public sector employee, who discloses public interest information to a proper authority and may suffer reprisal for it, and who may claim in tort or under the Equal Opportunity Act 1984, seek an injunction or relocation (pid-discloser.l4)

scope: The informant's disclosure, protection and claims, from the informant's seat. In: s 3 (public interest information, detrimental action; public authority, public officer, public sector contractor as choices); ss 5, 6, 7A, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12(1), (3), (4), (5A); Part 3 (ss 13, 14, 15A, 15B, 15, 16, 17, 18A); s 23(1)(a), (b) as named; ss 24, 25. Out: ss 1, 2, 4, 26, 27, 28, Schedule 1 (machinery); s 9 (the authority's action, and the subject's right to make a submission); ss 11(3), 12(2) (other Acts' procedure); Part 4 (ss 18-22, the Public Sector Commissioner); s 23 otherwise; the measure of damages and the limitation period for the s 15 tort (not in the Act). Reasons in NOTES.md.
